searchText: Hey @here Im not sure which channel to ask this so i'll ask it here. I have a question on EIP-1559 hoping someone can clarify it for me. Based on this blog: https://hackmd.io/@tvanepps/1559-wallets How gas fees are determined for ETH2 is that if the previous block is more than 50% full, it will increase the gas fees by 12.5%, if less than 50% full, it will decrease gas fees by 12.5%, and is block is 50% full, gas fees remain same. Then there is an example of 100% and 0% where gas fees increase and decrease respectively. So if block is 51% on every block, gas fees will just keep increasing by 12.5% continuously? This doesn't seem right, I think I am missing something here 😅 No, 51% means only a small increase, not 12.5% oh, how is the percentage increase determined then? Is there a breakdown somewhere I can read on? https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1559, see the if-elif-else near `# check if the base fee is correct` It's just linear, so 51% full would mean a 2% of 12.5% = 0.25% increase in base fee. Definitely check for yourself by plugging in some numbers though 🙂 2% is the ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER ? No, 2% is how far between 50 and 100% full a 51%-full block is <@749169437982326785> friendly heads up, if you are unsure next time <#595721451651465227> is a better channel.
